question_text:
Two children of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are standing in equilibrium as shown in figure, on a uniform rod at constant speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ respectively. Then they start moving simultaneously on the rod. Consider the following statements about the motion of the two children.
For the equilibrium to be maintained at any time $t$,

options.option_text: they should always move in opposite directions.
the rate of change of the momentum always equal to zero.
they should move so that the moment produced by one child about $O$ is always equal and opposite to the moment produced by the other child about $O$.
only A, B and C are true.
only B and C are true.
